motivation: A complete non-truncated Edge-6 response used one syntactically valid s_<24hex> identifier that was absent from the public dossier. Treating that one citation as a batch transport failure discarded four other questions and conflated evidence hallucination with serialization validity.

transport_or_envelope_failure: wrong or missing request-bound question set
foreign query IDs or foreign decision nodes
semantic_evidence_failure: a syntactically valid span-shaped ID absent from documents[].spans[].span_id
an evidence edge incident to such an unknown span-shaped ID

frozen_scoring_policy.positive_unknown_span: one false positive in minimal evidence-span precision and an exact-match failure for that question
frozen_scoring_policy.rejected_unknown_span: one false positive in rejected-evidence precision and an exact-match failure for that question
frozen_scoring_policy.edge_touching_unknown_span: one false positive typed edge; missing intended gold edge remains one false negative

closed_world_schema_decision.reason: An enum would add roughly 24k schema characters per match and may force or mask exact-copy behavior. Exact citation is part of evidence grounding and must remain measurable rather than decoder-corrected.

dataset_change_authority.rationale: The public span exists and is unambiguous; the observed failure is exact citation rather than a data contradiction.

acceptance_gates: unknown span IDs are retained verbatim under semantic_false_positive_v2
foreign query and decision nodes remain protocol-invalid
scorer counts unknown citations and incident edges as false positives
affected and unaffected questions are both scoreable
runner metadata records semantic warnings without marking the batch invalid
historical Edge-6 artifacts remain invalid and unmodified
all existing tests plus new mutation tests pass
